title: Suffering and the problem of evil
tagline: Face the hardest question: if God is good, why is there so much pain?
whyItMatters: Suffering is the most common reason people give for doubting God. A good answer must be honest about pain and not only clever.

mindset.tip: Do not argue with someone in fresh grief; sit with them first.
Separate the personal question ("why me?") from the philosophical one ("is God possible?"); they need different answers.
Admit what we do not know; the Church says plainly that this is a mystery (CCC 309).
Point to the cross: God did not stay outside suffering (Hebrews 4:15; CCC 312, 1505).

levels.title: Foundations
levels.goal: Know the problem and the Church's basic reply.

steps.why: Start with the app's answer to "If God is good, why is there evil?".
And its answer to "Why does God allow suffering?".
A short, clear reply that evil does not disprove God.
A gentle talk about God in our pain.
Four practical ways Christians face suffering.
Catechism lesson: why does a good God allow suffering?

steps.prompt: What would you want someone to say, and not say, if you were in a time of deep loss?

levels.title: Making the case
levels.goal: Understand the main Christian replies: freedom, a world of goods, and the cross.

steps.why: Lay out the problem and the standard replies.
See God's own answer in Christ.
Hear Aquinas, the Holocaust and the cross discussed.
Distinguish what God causes from what he allows.
Read the Bible's own long argument about the suffering of the innocent.
The sourced case that the cross is God's answer.
Why the Church links the world's brokenness to the Fall.

levels.title: Objections and replies
levels.goal: Meet the strongest forms of the objection and answer them with respect.

steps.why: The charge that the Church says suffering is God's punishment.
Hear the problem of evil turned into a fair conversation.
Watch a bishop face the question in a debate with an atheist.
See how a pope speaks at the site of the worst evil of the century.
Read a neutral account of the argument from evil.
Read about hope that survives suffering (nos. 35-40).
A lesson on suffering that is not wasted.

levels.title: Going deeper
levels.goal: Read the classic treatments and the strongest literary protest.

steps.why: Boethius in prison asks why the wicked prosper (Book IV).
Augustine on evil as the lack of good.
Aquinas on what evil is.
Aquinas on providence and freedom.
John Paul II's letter on the Christian meaning of suffering.
Read Ivan's protest, the strongest atheist case in literature.
Augustine on the creation of the angels and the origin of two cities.
The early heresy that answered evil with two gods, and why the Church said no.
